To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GABAB receptors differentially modulate the hilar interneurons to enhance granule cells output.

the two main GABAB receptor subunits are expressed in the dendritic and axonal compartments of the DG, respectively, and that these two subunits differentially control synaptic inhibition in the DG to enhance GC output.

GABAB(2) and GABA1a receptors are expressed on different compartments of DG neurons and that the two receptors have opposite functions in the DG: GABAB2 enhances GC output, while GABAB(IA) inhibits it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the GABAB receptor-mediated disinhibition in the dentate granule cells and how this disinhibition is differentially regulated by the two GABAB receptor subunit combinations.
the role of GABAB(2) receptors in the dentato-hippocampal circuitry, and how they are involved in the modulation of synaptic inhibition in the granule cell layer.
the role of GABAB receptor subunits in the DG, with a particular focus on their expression, function, and modulation of synaptic inhibition in the DG.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GABA-B1a and GABA-B1b receptors are differentially involved in modulating synaptic inhibition in the DG, with the GABA-B1-b receptor being more important in the modulation of synaptic inhibition in the molecular layer, while the GABA-B-1a receptor being more important for the modulation of synaptic transmission in the hilar region
GABAB(2) receptors are the most important for the GABAB-mediated enhancement of granule cell excitability in the DG.
GABAB receptors are expressed at all levels of the DG, and their activation enhances the excitatory output of the hippocampus by reducing synaptic inhibition in the GCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GABAB(2) subtype is expressed on the axonal terminals of hilar interneurons and is responsible for the GABAB receptor-mediated enhancement of perforant pathway input, whereas GABAB(3) is expressed on dendrites and is responsible for reducing inhibition of GCs.
the GABAB(2) subtype is the predominant receptor in the DG, while the GABAB (1a,2), GABAB(3) and GABAR(1) subtypes have a more limited expression.
GABA(B)1a receptors are the dominant subtype at the axon terminals of mossy cells and at the dendrites of hilar interneurons, whereas GABA(B)2 is expressed on the somata of mossy cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GABAB(2) is expressed at higher levels in the DG than GABAB(3).

the GABAB(2) receptor is expressed at the dendritic spines of the GCs and the hilar interneurons, and the GABAB receptor is expressed in the axons of hilar interneurons and the axon terminal boutons of the perforant path.
the GABAB(2) subunit is the most abundant subunit in the DG and that GABAB( 1b, 2) and GABA B(1a, 2) receptors are differentially distributed in the hilar region.
